newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-weak -dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs seen steady-weak -dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices Friday were seen steady with a weak tone, in light trading ahead of the Memorial Day holiday weekend, livestock dealers said.
Buying interest was expected to be sparse, with several packer buyers saying they had enough hogs earmarked for Friday delivery.
Demand also was seen light because of expected low slaughter on Saturday. Major U.S. hog plants also will be closed on Monday in observance of Memorial Day, they said.
Outlooks for lower prices following the holiday also could weigh on cash hog values Friday, dealers said.
Hog prices on Tuesday were seen pressured by an expected back-up of nearby supplies because of the holiday. The back-up could take several days to work through, they said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top prices for hogs to be delivered to plants were seen at $59.50 per cwt and Illinois top prices at plants were seen at $59.00, dealers there said.
Indiana/Ohio top prices for hogs were projected unchanged at $59.00, they said.
